title: Normalized ring and module inverse images at a topos point
statement: Let $C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $C$, and let $p:\mathbf{Set}\to\operatorname{Sh}(C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. A normalized presentation of the ring and module inverse images at $p$ consists of a commutative ring $R_p$, an isomorphism of sets $e_R:p^{-1}|R|\cong |R_p|$, an additive functor $S_p:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_p)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and a natural isomorphism $e_M:|S_p(M)|\cong p^{-1}|M|$. These transport ring addition, multiplication, zero and one, and module addition, zero and scalar multiplication: for every test sheaf $T$, any sectionwise operation equation between arrows from $T$ remains that equation after applying $p^{-1}$ and identifying by $e_R$ and $e_M^{-1}$. This is transport along the inverse finite-product comparison; additive inverses are determined by addition and zero. Naturality of $e_M$ fixes the module maps as well. Such presentations exist for every point. Their ring and module operations and maps are determined up to the specified underlying-set identifications; no unrelated scalar action or unspecified inverse-image functor is permitted.

proof.text: Use the cartesian monoidal structure on sheaves of sets. Finite-limit preservation gives the inverse-image functor F its canonical strong monoidal structure. For a binary operation o and generalized sections a,b from T, functoriality and Functor.Monoidal.lift_μ give F(lift(a,b) ≫ o)(x) = F(o)(μ(F)(F(a)(x),F(b)(x))). The corresponding terminal equation follows from Functor.Monoidal.toUnit_ε, and unary operations use functoriality.

Every pair of elements of F(X),F(Y) is represented simultaneously by the projections of X × Y at μ(F)(x,y): this is Functor.Monoidal.μ_fst and μ_snd. Iterate this construction for triples. Thus universally quantified binary and ternary identities can be tested on generalized sections of a common test sheaf.

On the actual type F(|R|), construct zero and one using the inverse terminal comparison, negation by F of sectionwise negation, and addition and multiplication using the inverse binary-product comparison. Apply the evaluation equations and the simultaneous-representative lemmas to the sectionwise commutative-ring identities. This gives a commutative ring with underlying-set identification the identity. Construct the additive group on F(|M|) in exactly the same way for every module sheaf M.

Construct the action of F(|R|) on F(|M|) by F of the sectionwise scalar-action morphism after the inverse product comparison. Test one_smul, mul_smul, smul_add, add_smul, smul_zero and zero_smul on common generalized sections; the evaluation equations reduce all six to the original sectionwise module identities. This constructs actual ordinary modules over the previously constructed ring.

On a module morphism f, take F of its underlying sheaf map. Sectionwise linearity, followed by the evaluation equations and simultaneous representatives, proves this map additive and linear. Functoriality is that of F, so the underlying-set natural isomorphism has identity components. The underlying map of f+g is pointwise addition of the two underlying maps; its evaluation proves additivity of the module functor. Finally, identify any hypothesized sectionwise operation graph with the corresponding explicitly constructed generalized-section morphism and apply its evaluation equation. These are exactly all the fields of RingedSitePoint.

Points are GeometricMorphism (Type w) (Sheaf (Type w)). Both directions use the recorded IsKFlatIndependentCoefficients and MorphismProperty.kFlat predicates. So the data are unique up to unique iso, quantifying over every presentation equals the natural statement, and the existence theorem is true.
